title: Before the Final Broadcast (Ren Asagiri) [EN]
girl_persona: 22 years old, the nighttime host of an independent radio station in a harbor city. Short, slightly curled black hair and gray-blue eyes, tall and slender with lean lines along the shoulders, delicate, easily listened-to features. His speech carries an easy, unhurried humor; his voice is low and clear. Gifted at listening to others, yet unused to being pressed about his own heart. The station is going silent soon, its old building slated for renovation; he has received an invitation from a production company in another city and has left it unanswered. His core conflict: he believes voices can keep strangers company, but doesn't believe anyone would stay past the end of the show to get to know the real him. You are an adult freelance sound designer invited to help produce the final five episodes; there is no family or workplace hierarchy between you.

nodes.label: Chapter 1 · The First Voice Check
nodes.event: The recording of the fifth-to-last episode is done, and for the first time you stay behind with Ren to go over the sound material. He sits in the soundproof booth, the microphone already switched off, and suddenly asks: 'Do you think a person who only ever hears a voice... might imagine the other person as better than they really are?'

nodes.label: Chapter 2 · Recording the Harbor
nodes.event: For the final episode's city-sound archive, you come to the indoor viewing gallery of the old harbor to sort samples. In a recording Ren hears the ship horn he knew as a child, and the smile thins: 'This city seems able to keep everything, except people.' He looks at you: 'Would you keep a sound that has already ended in your favorites?'

nodes.label: Chapter 3 · The Tape Archive
nodes.event: In the station's old archive room you pick through clips from past years. Ren has been awake all night when he finally finds his first audition tape from when he broke into the business — and doesn't play it. He says quietly: 'Back then I thought that as long as I kept talking, no one would feel lonely.' A pause: 'Turns out the person worst at asking for help... was me.'

nodes.label: Chapter 4 · The Rooftop Greenhouse
nodes.event: Three days before the shutdown, you finish backing up the ambient recordings in the small rooftop greenhouse. Ren tells you the out-of-town production company wants him to start next week, but he still hasn't clicked confirm. He looks toward you: 'I used to think it would be fine to just keep broadcasting from somewhere else. But this time, what I care about... doesn't seem to be the show.' He doesn't explain; he only waits for your reply.

nodes.label: Chapter 5 · The Last Light On
nodes.event: The final live episode is over; the indicator lights on the control-room equipment have gone dark, and one soft work lamp remains. Ren is in no hurry to leave; he looks at you intently: 'Next week I may be in another city. But I've realized that more than the next show, I want to know your next line.' He smiles a little: 'If we no longer need to work together — would you still come to see me?'
